personal_stories.fullContent:
Starting a Roth IRA as a teenager can be a great way to save for retirement and build wealth over time. A Roth IRA is a type of individual retirement account that allows you to contribute after-tax dollars, which can then grow tax-free. This means that you won't have to pay taxes on the money when you withdraw it in retirement, which can be a significant advantage.

How to Start a Roth IRA

To start a Roth IRA, you'll need to open an account with a financial institution, such as a bank or investment firm. You'll then need to contribute money to the account, which can be done on a regular basis, such as monthly or annually.

The annual contribution limit for a Roth IRA is $6,000 in 2026, and you can contribute as much or as little as you want, as long as you don't exceed the limit.

Action Step

One specific thing you can do this week is to research and open a Roth IRA account, and start contributing to it on a regular basis. This can be a great way to build wealth over time and provide a head start on saving for retirement.

To build an emergency savings fund, you'll need to start by setting aside a portion of your income each month, which can be done by setting up automatic transfers from your checking account to your savings account.
